title: Medication safety (MSDS)
summary: Medication safety - who may prescribe, verbal and telephone orders with the prescriber's countersignature, the pharmacist's queries on unclear orders, high-alert and look-alike medicines with a second person's check at the counter and at the bedside, identity wristbands and the checks before every dose, labels, batch recalls, expired ward stock, self-administration, the patient's own medicines, the written policy and the statistics.
markdown:
# Medication safety (MSDS)

The Punjab Healthcare Commission's Minimum Service Delivery Standards (MSDS) give medication 21 indicators (MOM 51-71)
and patient identification two more (AAC 30, COP 37). Surveyors read the policies, then sample ten inpatient records
and watch nurses and pharmacists at work; most indicators are "not met" after a single failure. What the system does
for each:

| MSDS | What is checked | Haspataal |
|---|---|---|
| 51, 54 | Orders written clearly, dated, timed, signed; what happens when one is unclear | Structured e-prescriptions with the prescriber's stamp; the pharmacist's **query** blocks the line until a doctor answers |
| 52 | Who may prescribe; restricted classes | A PMDC doctor, or the **Prescribing** privilege; **restricted** medicines need **RestrictedPrescribing** (database) |
| 53 | Orders in one place in the record | The prescription of the visit or the admission |
| 55 | Verbal orders written down, read back, countersigned | **Verbal/telephone orders** by the nurse, read back, countersigned by the prescriber in time (reminder, review) |
| 56, 57 | A list of high-alert and look-alike medicines, displayed; verified before dispensing and giving | **High-alert categories** and **look-alike pairs** on every screen; a **second person** co-signs at the counter and at the bedside (database) |
| 58-60 | Safe dispensing, recalls, no expired medicine | FEFO; expired and **recalled** batches never issued, in the pharmacy or from ward stock; the **recall register**; expired ward stock removed |
| 61, 63 | Labels | A **label per medicine** dispensed; the **label of a prepared dose** |
| 62 | Given only by those permitted by law | A registered nurse (PNC) or doctor (PMDC), or the **MedicationAdministration** privilege (database) |
| 64-68, AAC 30 | Patient identified; medicine, dose, route and time checked before a dose | **Wristbands**; the chart needs the band scanned (or two identifiers), checks the medicine's barcode, and a reason for another dose, route or time |
| 69 | Every dose documented | The MAR (every due dose charted: record review ADM_MAR) |
| 70 | Self-administration | The doctor allows it per line; the nurse charts each dose |
| 71 | Medicines brought from outside | Recorded, identified by the pharmacist, kept, **handed back before the ward clears the discharge** (database) |
| COP 37 | Identity before the anaesthetic | The sign in of the safety checklist records the band scan (or two identifiers) |

Who does what:

* **Doctors** (`prescription.create`): prescribe; countersign their verbal orders; answer the pharmacist's queries.
* **Ward nurses** (`prescription.verbal.record`, `patient.wristband.print`, `patient.own_medicine.record`,
  `ipd.mar.administer`, `medication.double_check`): verbal orders, wristbands, own medicines, the checks before a dose,
  the second check of a colleague's high-alert dose. **ER nurses** (`prescription.verbal.record`,
  `patient.wristband.print`, `medication.double_check`): verbal orders, wristbands, the second check. The **admission desk** prints wristbands too.
* **Pharmacists** (`prescription.query.raise`, `patient.own_medicine.identify`, `medication.double_check`): queries,
  identifying own medicines, the second check at the counter.
* **Pharmacy admin** (`medication.safety.configure`, `pharmacy.recall.manage`): the lists, recalls.
* **Quality Officer, Owner** (`medication.statistics.view`): the statistics, the policy.

## 1. The lists and the policy (pharmacy admin)

1. Flag the formulary: `PATCH /medication-safety/drugs/{drug_id}` with `high_alert_category` (`ConcentratedElectrolyte`,
   `Chemotherapy`, `Anticoagulant`, `Insulin`, `Opioid`, `Sedative`, `NeuromuscularBlocker`, `Inotrope`,
   `Thrombolytic`, `Psychotropic`, `HighCost`, `Other`; `null` clears it) and `is_restricted`. A new drug can carry them
   from `POST /pharmacy-admin/drugs`. A high-alert medicine is never sold over the counter (`VALIDATION_ERROR`).
2. Pair look-alikes: `POST /medication-safety/lasa-pairs {"drug_id", "other_drug_id", "note"}` (the note says how to
   tell them apart); `PATCH /medication-safety/lasa-pairs/{pair_id}` changes the note or retires the pair
   (`is_active: false`).
3. `GET /medication-safety/high-alert-list` (screen) and `GET /medication-safety/high-alert-list/pdf`: print it for
   every nursing station and the pharmacy, again after every change (MSDS 56 ii).
4. `GET /medication-safety/policy/pdf`: the written medication policy generated from what the system enforces, with
   lines for the medical director's and the chief pharmacist's approval (MSDS 51, 55, 57-61, 63, 70, 71).
5. Privileges (the [clinical privileges register](surgical-care.md), `POST /ot/privileges`): `Prescribing` for
   a clinician other than a PMDC doctor who may prescribe (e.g. a nurse-midwife, within its scope),
   `RestrictedPrescribing` for the restricted medicines, `MedicationAdministration` for staff other than registered
   nurses and doctors who may give medicines.

Every medicine the formulary search returns (`GET /drugs/search`) carries `high_alert_category`, `is_restricted` and
`lasa_with` (the names it looks or sounds like); so do the lines of a prescription and the doses of the MAR. Show a red
badge for high-alert and a "looks like …" warning.

## 2. Prescribing (doctor)

`POST /prescriptions` as in [clinical and prescriptions](clinical-and-prescriptions.md), plus:

* The caller must be allowed to prescribe (`PRESCRIBER_NOT_AUTHORIZED`), and to prescribe a restricted medicine.
* `self_administration: true` on an inpatient's oral, inhaled or topical medicine that is not high-alert lets the
  patient take it themselves (MSDS 70; `SELF_ADMINISTRATION_INVALID` otherwise). Explain it to the patient. It applies
  to a medicine bought outside too (an `ExternalMarket` prescription, decisions 59) when the line names a drug of the
  hospital's list (`drug_id`), so that its high-alert check applies; a typed `external_drug_name` is never
  self-administered.

## 3. Verbal and telephone orders (nurse → doctor)

Only in an emergency or when the doctor cannot write, for an inpatient or an emergency patient; never for an
outpatient, never chemotherapy (`VERBAL_ORDER_INVALID`).

1. The nurse writes it down at once and reads it back: `POST /prescriptions/verbal` with `Idempotency-Key`:
   ```json
   { "prescriber_id": 12, "order_mode": "Telephone", "read_back": true, "admission_id": 301,
     "items": [ { "drug_id": 5, "qty_prescribed": 2, "dose_text": "1 g", "route": "IV", "frequency_code": "BD",
                  "interval_hours": 12, "start_at": "2026-09-30T22:00:00+05:00" } ] }
   ```
   An emergency patient without an admission: `ticket_id` of the ER visit instead of `admission_id`. The order goes to
   the pharmacy and the MAR like a written one, stamped with the doctor's name; `received_by` is the nurse.
   The prescriber from `GET /staff/lookup?license_type=PMDC`. A verbal order is not part of a consultation note: leave
   `encounter_id` out (decision 62).
2. The doctor is told (`medication.order.updated` to their screens) and countersigns:
   `POST /prescriptions/{prescription_id}/countersign` (only the prescriber, once: `VERBAL_ORDER_COUNTERSIGN_INVALID`).
3. `GET /verbal-orders` (`mine`, `pending`, `admission_id`): `is_overdue` once `verbal_order_countersign_hours` (24) have
   passed; the worker job `medication.alerts` reminds the prescriber once (a notification); the record review counts
   every late or missing countersignature (ADM_VERBAL_ORDERS).

## 4. The pharmacist's query (pharmacist ↔ doctor)

1. An unclear or unsafe order is not dispensed: `POST /prescriptions/{prescription_id}/queries`
   `{"prescription_item_id": 77, "reason": "ChildDose", "question": "Adult dose for a 4-year-old (14 kg)?"}`
   (`prescription_item_id` null: the whole prescription). Reasons: `Unclear`, `DoseOrFrequency`, `Allergy`,
   `Interaction`, `Duplicate`, `ChildDose`, `Restricted`, `WrongPatient`, `Other`. One open query per line
   (`PRESCRIPTION_QUERY_OPEN`). The prescriber gets a notification.
2. While it is open the line cannot be dispensed (`PRESCRIPTION_QUERY_OPEN`); the queue shows `open_queries`.
3. A doctor who may prescribe answers: `POST /prescription-queries/{query_id}/answer`
   `{"outcome": "ConfirmedAsWritten", "answer": "…"}`, or `"Changed"` after stopping the line
   (`POST /prescriptions/{id}/items/{item_id}/stop`) or cancelling the prescription and writing the new order
   (`PRESCRIPTION_QUERY_STATE_INVALID` otherwise). The answer carries the doctor's stamp; the pharmacist is notified.
4. `GET /prescription-queries` (`status`, `mine` for the doctor's own orders, `prescription_id`);
   `POST /prescription-queries/{query_id}/withdraw` for a query raised by mistake. `GET /prescriptions/{id}` lists
   `queries`.

## 5. Dispensing a high-alert medicine, and the labels (pharmacist)

1. `POST /prescriptions/{id}/dispense` as usual; a line of a high-alert medicine needs the second person's check: they
   check the order and the medicine and type their credentials:
   ```json
   { "items": [ { "prescription_item_id": 9 } ], "checker_username": "usman", "checker_password": "••••" }
   ```
   Without it `HIGH_ALERT_CHECK_REQUIRED`; the same person `DUAL_CONTROL_SAME_PERSON`. The dispensation records
   `checked_by`. Recalled batches are never picked.
2. Print one label per medicine: `GET /dispensations/{dispensation_id}/labels` → print payloads for the label printer:
   the patient, the medicine (brand and generic) and strength, `directions` (dose, route, frequency, duration,
   instructions), the prescriber, the date, the batch and expiry, `warnings` (high-alert, look-alike).

## 6. Wristbands (admission desk, ward, ER)

1. `POST /wristbands {"admission_id": 301}` (or `{"er_visit_id": 88}`) → `wristband` and `print` (label printer: name,
   MRN as a barcode and QR code `HMS:PT:<mrn>`, age and sex, the admission or ER number, ward and bed; `allergies`
   printed prominently). A patient who already wears one: `replacement_reason` required (damaged, cut off for a
   cannula, details corrected); the last band is marked replaced.
2. `GET /wristbands?admission_id=…` (the register, `is_current`); reprint the same band after a printer jam:
   `GET /wristbands/{wristband_id}/print-payload`.
3. Scan to verify on any screen that treats or samples a patient: `GET /wristbands/verify?code=…&admission_id=…` →
   `match`; false: stop, `scanned_patient` says whose band it is.
4. The worklist lists patients without a band (`NoWristband`); the record review checks one was worn (ADM_WRISTBAND).

The theatre sign in records the identity check too ([surgical care](surgical-care.md)): `wristband_code` (or
`identity_check: "TwoIdentifiers"`) in `POST /ot/bookings/{booking_id}/safety-checks` with `phase: "SignIn"`.

## 7. Giving a dose (ward nurse)

`POST /mar/{mar_id}/chart` (or `POST /admissions/{id}/mar/prn`) with `status: "Administered"` walks the rights:

```json
{ "status": "Administered", "wristband_code": "MRN-2026-000123", "drug_barcode": "8964000100093",
  "second_checker_username": "hina", "second_checker_password": "••••",
  "dose_given_text": "10 mmol", "route_given": "IV", "variance_reason": null }
```

* **The patient**: `wristband_code` as scanned (`PATIENT_IDENTITY_MISMATCH`: another patient's band, stop). No scanner:
  `identity_check: "TwoIdentifiers"` after asking the name and the date of birth or MRN. An emergency or Code Red patient
  who cannot be identified yet: `"EmergencyOverride"` with `identity_note`. Nothing: `PATIENT_IDENTITY_REQUIRED`.
* **The medicine**: `drug_barcode` as scanned from the pack (`DRUG_MISMATCH`: stop), else it counts as checked by eye.
* **A high-alert medicine**: a second nurse or doctor checks independently and co-signs
  (`HIGH_ALERT_CHECK_REQUIRED`; a colleague without a registration: `ADMINISTRATION_NOT_AUTHORIZED`).
* **The dose, route and time**: default the order's; another dose or route, or more than `mar_on_time_window_minutes`
  (60) from the scheduled time, needs `variance_reason` (`ADMINISTRATION_VARIANCE_REASON_REQUIRED`).
* **Who gives it**: a registered nurse (PNC) or doctor (PMDC), or the MedicationAdministration privilege
  (`ADMINISTRATION_NOT_AUTHORIZED`).
* `self_administered: true` for a line the doctor allowed (`self_administration`).
* From ward stock (`ward_stock_batch_id`): never an expired (`BATCH_EXPIRED`) or recalled (`BATCH_RECALLED`) batch.

Before drawing up an injection or an infusion: `POST /mar/{mar_id}/prepare {"preparation": "in 100 ml normal saline
over 30 minutes"}` → the label to stick on the syringe or bag (MSDS 63), once per dose. A label lost or never printed
(the app restarted, the printer failed): `GET /mar/{mar_id}/dose-label` prints it again from what the preparation
recorded, marked REPRINT (`fields.reprint`); it prepares and gives nothing (`DOSE_NOT_PREPARED` before the
preparation).

`GET /admissions/{id}/mar` shows per dose `identity_check`, `drug_check`, `second_checked_by_name`, `variance_reason`,
`prepared_at` and the medicine's `high_alert_category` and `lasa_with`.

## 8. Recalls (pharmacy admin)

1. `POST /drug-recalls` with `Idempotency-Key`:
   ```json
   { "drug_id": 5, "batch_ids": [41], "source": "DRAP", "reference": "DRAP alert 12/2026", "recall_class": "ClassII",
     "reason": "Particulate matter in vials", "contact_patients": true }
   ```
   (`all_batches: true` for every batch.) At once the batches are blocked: FEFO skips them and the database refuses to
   dispense them, send them to a ward, use them in theatre or give a dose from ward stock (`BATCH_RECALLED`). The wards
   and the pharmacy get a critical notification; screens refresh on `pharmacy.recall.updated`.
   The medicine from `GET /drugs/search`.
2. `GET /drug-recalls/{recall_id}`: per batch what is left in the pharmacy and on the wards and what was dispensed,
   given and used in theatre; the wards holding it; the `patients` who received it (patients with their mobile, named
   walk-in customers and staff), with each `source`.
3. `POST /drug-recalls/{recall_id}/remove-stock {"note": "Destroyed as DRAP directs"}` writes off every unit left
   (again later if more turns up). Stock the supplier takes back goes as a return instead, so its credit is not lost:
   `POST /pharmacy-admin/batches/{batch_id}/supplier-returns {"reason": "Recall", "recall_id": …}` for each batch
   ([back office](clinical-and-prescriptions.md)); the recall can close once no stock is left either way.
4. `PATCH /drug-recalls/{recall_id}/patients/{recall_patient_id} {"outcome": "Contacted", "note": "…"}`
   (`Unreachable`, `NotNeeded` with the reason).
5. `POST /drug-recalls/{recall_id}/close {"note"}` once `can_close` (`RECALL_NOT_COMPLETE` with the counts). Opened by
   mistake: `POST /drug-recalls/{recall_id}/cancel {"reason"}` releases the batches.
6. `GET /drug-recalls` (`status`, `drug_id`): the register the surveyor asks for (MSDS 59).

## 9. Expired ward stock (head nurse)

`GET /wards/{ward_id}/inventory` flags `is_expired` and `is_recalled`; the worklist lists `ExpiredWardStock`. Remove
it: `POST /wards/{ward_id}/inventory/remove {"batch_id", "qty", "reason": "Expiry", "note"}` (`Damage` too: written
off; `ReturnToPharmacy`: unexpired, unrecalled stock back on the pharmacy's shelves).

## 10. The patient's own medicines (ward nurse, pharmacist)

1. On arrival: `POST /admissions/{id}/own-medicines`
   ```json
   { "brought_by": "Son, Kamran", "stored_at": "Ward",
     "medicines": [ { "medicine_name": "Metformin", "strength": "500 mg", "quantity": "1 strip, 6 tablets left",
                      "batch_no": "MF2231", "expiry_date": "2027-06-30" } ] }
   ```
   They are kept and **not used** during the stay: the doctor orders what the patient needs and the pharmacy supplies
   it. `GET /admissions/{id}/own-medicines` (the doctor sees them as the medication history).
2. The pharmacist identifies each (worklist `OwnMedicineToIdentify`): `POST /own-medicines/{id}/identify
   {"identification": "Identified", "drug_id": 5, "stored_at": "Pharmacy"}` (`NotIdentifiable`, `Expired`, `Damaged`).
3. Before the patient leaves: `POST /admissions/{id}/own-medicines/hand-back {"handed_to": "Son, Kamran"}` (all still
   held, or `own_medicine_ids`), or `POST /own-medicines/{id}/destroy {"reason", "witness"}` with the patient's
   agreement. The ward's discharge clearance (`NursingMARVerification`) waits for this (`OWN_MEDICINES_HELD` with
   `details.medicines`); the worklist shows `OwnMedicineToHandBack`.

## 11. The worklist and the statistics

* `GET /medication-safety/worklist` (`ward_id`; `mine`: the caller's verbal orders and queries only): verbal orders to
  countersign, open queries, patients without a wristband, own medicines to identify and to hand back, open recalls,
  expired ward stock; `is_overdue` in red. The admissions desk (`patient.wristband.print` without
  `medication.safety.view`) gets the patients without a wristband only.
* `GET /medication-safety/statistics?date_from=…&date_to=…` (`medication.statistics.view`): `measures` with the MSDS
  indicator each evidences (verbal orders countersigned in time, high-alert doses and dispensing double-checked, doses
  after a wristband scan and a medicine scan, doses on time, due doses charted, admissions with a wristband, own
  medicines handed back), doses by identity and medicine check, variances, the queries by reason and outcome, the
  recalls.
* The medical record review checks each admission automatically: ADM_WRISTBAND, ADM_MAR, ADM_VERBAL_ORDERS,
  ADM_OWN_MEDICINES ([medical record review](medical-record-review.md)).

## 12. The storage log (pharmacist, ward nurse)

MSDS MOM 58 and the web portal's CPSA 10.3 ask for the temperature (and humidity) of every place medicines are kept, recorded
twice a day, with the action taken when a reading is out of range.

1. `POST /pharmacy/storage-checks` (`pharmacy.storage.record`: pharmacists, pharmacy admins, ward and head nurses)
   ```json
   { "storage_area": "Ward 2 refrigerator", "storage_kind": "Refrigerator", "ward_id": 3, "temperature_c": 9.5,
     "action_taken": "Door found ajar: closed; insulin checked, nothing discarded" }
   ```
   Keep one spelling per place (the register groups by `storage_area`). The limits are the settings of the `storage_kind`
   (Room, Refrigerator, Freezer, ColdChainBox) unless `min_c` / `max_c` are given for a place with its own range. Out of
   range without `action_taken`: `STORAGE_CHECK_ACTION_REQUIRED`; with it the reading is kept, the row shows red and the
   event `pharmacy.storage.out_of_range` (priority high) reaches the pharmacists.
   The ward from `GET /beds/matrix?include_beds=false` (none for the pharmacy).
2. `GET /pharmacy/storage-checks?date_from=&date_to=&storage_area=%fridge%&ward_id=&out_of_range_only=` (the log),
   `GET /pharmacy/storage-checks/summary` (per area: readings, out of range, lowest and highest, the days with the full
   twice-a-day routine: a day with one reading or none is a gap to explain to the surveyor) and
   `GET /pharmacy/storage-checks/register/pdf` (the register of the period); readers: `pharmacy.stock.view`,
   `medication.safety.view` or `pharmacy.storage.record`.

## Settings

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `verbal_order_countersign_hours` | 24 | a verbal order not countersigned by then is overdue: the prescriber is reminded once |
| `mar_on_time_window_minutes` | 60 | a scheduled dose given further from its time needs a reason |
| `pharmacy_room_min_c`, `pharmacy_room_max_c` | 10, 25 | the acceptable readings of a room or cupboard |
| `pharmacy_fridge_min_c`, `pharmacy_fridge_max_c` | 2, 8 | the acceptable readings of a medicine refrigerator or cold-chain box |
| `pharmacy_freezer_min_c`, `pharmacy_freezer_max_c` | -30, -15 | the acceptable readings of a medicine freezer |
